paper: measured here - RTX 5090, pi0.5 on LIBERO
tagline: why fewer, larger kernels beat more, smaller ones
source: Measured on one machine: RTX 5090, pi0.5 on LIBERO spatial task 0, closed loop, median of 50 decisions after 8 warm calls. Utilisation from Nsight Compute, duration-weighted.

panels.title: Why a kernel launch costs what it costs
panels.sub: every kernel reads its operands from device memory and writes its result back, so one launch is one round trip
panels.note: a fused kernel keeps between its stages what an unfused pair would have sent home and fetched again

panels.title: The same decision, cut into fewer pieces
panels.sub: both arms compute the same action chunk from the same observation, and one of them asks the GPU for it five times fewer
panels.note: same work, fewer trips - so each of ours carries five times as much
panels.tail: the same length of work, cut differently
panels.scale: one drawn block is 100 kernel launches

panels.title: What it came to
